newsitem.title: USA: Sonat makes 4th Pinnacle Reef natgas find.
newsitem.headline: Sonat makes 4th Pinnacle Reef natgas find.

text.p: Sonat Inc said Tuesday it has completed drilling of its fourth Pinnacle Reef natural gas discovery in the Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef Trend in Leon County, Texas.
The company also said present plans call for its Sonat Exploration Co subsidiary to maintain its current level of drilling activity in the Pinnacle Reef Trend throughout 1997.
Sonat said the Cook No. 3 was drilled to a total depth of 15,840 feet and encountered a gross thickness of 607 feet of reef limestone in the interval below 15,133 feet.

The additional wells include the Fountain No. 2 and Blanton No. 2, the Morris Lazy K No. 1 and the Moore No. 2. The Fountain and Blanton wells are the second wells in reefs discovered and put on production by Sonat in 1996 in the Bear Grass area of Leon and Limestone counties.

The Morris Lazy K No. 1 is the first reef exploratory test in the Marquez area of Leon County and is a joint well with Amoco Corp. The Moore No. 2 is the first Sonat exploratory well in the Donie area of Limestone County. The company has a 50 percent working interest and spokesman Bruce Connery was unable to name the other owner.

Based on geological and geophysical analysis of this result and the drilling characteristics of the well, Sonat said, "the company anticipates a very successful and productive natural gas well completion."

Completion operations will begin immediately with first production test results available in about three weeks. Sonat has a 50 percent working interest in the Cook No. 3, which is a farmout from American Conetra.
Including the Cook No. 3, the company said, it has five wells drilling toward Pinnacle Reef natural gas objectives.

Sonat said it will begin, in about two weeks, "a very significant Pinnacle Reef exploratory test in the Tri-Cities area of Henderson County, Texas." If successful, the Ryon No. 1 will extend Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef Trend gas production some 45 miles to the northeast. It will be 50 percent owned by Sonat and 30 percent by United Meridian Corp, with the rest held by private parties.

Sonat said it "is aggressively increasing its leasehold in areas thought to be of high potential for Pinnacle Reef production. During the past year the company increased its Reef Trend acreage by about 65 percent."

At the present time, the company has completed 3-D seismic acquisition and data processing on about 15 percent of its leasehold and has identified 35 3-D seismic-supported Pinnacle Reef anomalies on this acreage. Five of the 35 prospects have been drilled, resulting in four discoveries. The fifth well, the Blazek No. 4, will be re-entered and sidetracked later in the year after additional 3-D seismic evaluation.
